A Brazilian court has ordered Apple to tighten age controls on a casino-style app on the App Store, including requiring age verification before in-app purchases. Here are the details.

Brazil orders Apple to strengthen App Store age checks

According to Tilt, a court in São Paulo has approved an emergency injunction requiring Apple to restrict minors from accessing the "Casino Roulette: Roulettist" app.

The ruling comes after four children's and adolescents' rights groups filed a civil lawsuit in July, alleging that minors were able to download casino-style games from the App Store and buy virtual chips with real currency, despite Casino Roulette: Roulettist being rated 18+.

Tilt reported that the court gave Apple five days in its ruling to block new downloads of Casino Roulette: Roulettist by users registered as minors, and demanded "age verification for purchases of virtual chips with real currency to continue playing or expand the in-app experience".

In addition to targeting that specific app, the ruling also prohibits Apple from listing new apps with equivalent casino-style mechanics on the App Store without effective age controls.

According to Tilt, the court also ordered Apple to preserve all records related to the app and submit a technical report detailing the measures taken. The court also set a daily fine of 100,000 reais (approximately 19,500 US dollars) to penalise violations.

Tilt has reached out to Apple for comment on the matter, but received no response before publication.
